function.name: ha_history_get_current_time
function.description:
Returns the current date and time from the Home Assistant server (Sanzay).
Call this before making any time-based query when the user uses a relative or named time
expression: "last month", "this winter", "yesterday", "last year", "in april", "recently".
Do not rely on your training data to infer the current date — it will often be wrong.
Skip only if an absolute ISO date range has already been stated in this conversation.

function.name: ha_history_list_entities
function.description:
Lists Sanzay sensors that have historical data available.
Each result includes the entity_id, friendly name, room/area, unit, and sensor type.
Call this to find the correct entity_id before querying any sensor you don't already know.
Skip only if the entity_id was already resolved earlier in this conversation.
Also use for explicit sensor discovery or when a previous call returned an ambiguous match.
Binary sensors (motion, doors, presence) need domain="binary_sensor" — no statistics.
For location tracking use domain="device_tracker". For zones use domain="zone".

domain.description:
Filter by entity domain. Common values:
"sensor" — numeric/measurement sensors (temperature, energy, power).
"binary_sensor" — on/off sensors (motion, doors, windows).
"device_tracker" — person/phone location tracking.
"zone" — geographical zones (home, work, school…).
Leave empty to include all domains with statistics.

search.description:
Search terms matched against entity_id, friendly name, device name, area, device class, and unit.
Multiple space-separated words are treated as OR — an entity matches if ANY word appears in any field.
E.g. "temperature humidity" returns all temperature OR humidity sensors.
E.g. "power energy electricity" returns any entity matching at least one of those words.

include_state.description:
When true, adds the current state value to each result row. Default: false.
Useful when you need both the entity_id and its current value in one call.
For a single entity's full state details, prefer ha_history_get_state instead.

function.name: ha_history_get_state
function.description:
Returns the current state of any Sanzay entity.
Use for: "What is the temperature in the kitchen right now?",
"Is the front door open?", "Where is person X?", "Is the washing machine running?"
Works for all entity domains: sensor, binary_sensor, device_tracker, zone,
climate, switch, light, cover, media_player, etc.
Returns: current state value, unit, last changed time, and key attributes.
Call ha_history_list_entities first if you don't know the exact entity_id.

entity_id.description: Exact entity_id from ha_history_list_entities. Do not guess.

function.name: ha_history_get_sensor_stats
function.description:
Computes statistics for a Sanzay sensor measuring instantaneous values:
temperature, humidity, CO₂, pressure, illuminance, or power draw in Watts.
Use for: "What was the lowest temperature last night?", "Average humidity in April?",
"Warmest day last summer?", "How many days above 25°C?", "Which days had frost?",
"At what time of day is it usually hottest?", "Which day of the week is most humid?"
Do NOT use for energy consumption (kWh) → use ha_history_get_consumption.
Do NOT use for event counting → use ha_history_detect_sessions.

entity.description: Exact entity_id from ha_history_list_entities (e.g. "sensor.ruuvitag_fc8f_temperature"). Do not guess.

start_time.description: Period start. Formats: relative (7d/30d/24h/2w/1y), named ("last month"/"last week"/"yesterday"/"last summer"/"Q1"), or ISO ("2026-04-01"). Default: 30d.

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

aggregation.description:
"mean": average. "min": lowest. "max": highest. "median": middle value.
"count" (requires group_by + filter): counts per slot how many readings satisfied
  the filter condition. Returns "N/M" per slot — e.g. "18/30 days at 06:00 exceeded 21°C".
  Use for: "how many days at each hour exceeded 25°C?",
           "how many weeks on each day-of-week was humidity above 70%?"
Choose: "hottest" → "max", "coldest" → "min", "average/typical" → "mean",
"how many X had Y?" with group_by → "count".

interval.description:
"none": one value for the whole period (default).
"hour"/"day"/"week"/"month": time series — one value per bucket.
Required when using filter_operator/filter_value.
Cannot be used together with group_by.

group_by.description:
Groups all readings by a repeating time unit across the full period, then applies
the aggregation. Ideal for pattern questions:
"hour_of_day": 24 buckets (00:00–23:00) — "at what time of day is it usually hottest?"
"day_of_week": 7 buckets (Mon–Sun) — "which day of the week is most humid?"
Cannot be used with interval. filter_operator/filter_value work normally on top.

filter_operator.description:
Filter results to buckets where the aggregated value satisfies [op] filter_value.
Requires interval (not "none") or group_by. Response includes matching bucket count.
E.g. frost days: aggregation="min", filter_operator="<", filter_value=0

filter_value.description: Threshold for filter_operator. Required when filter_operator is set.

max_results.description: Applies to interval time-series only (not scalar or group_by). Default: 100. Pass "all" for the complete series. Response shows total count when capped.

function.name: ha_history_get_consumption
function.description:
Calculates how much energy, water, gas, or other resource was consumed or produced
in Sanzay over a time period.
Use for: "How much electricity did the car charger use in February?",
"Total electricity last month?", "Solar production last week?",
"Daily energy usage last week", "Compare grid import this April vs last April",
"Which days used more than 10 kWh?"
Always returns consumption (the change over the period), never raw meter readings.
Do NOT use for instantaneous sensors (temperature, power in Watts) → use ha_history_get_sensor_stats.

entity.description: Exact entity_id from ha_history_list_entities (look for type="cumulative"). E.g. "sensor.electricity_meter_kwh". Do not guess.

start_time.description: Period start. Formats: relative (7d/30d/24h/2w/1y), named ("last month"/"last week"/"yesterday"/"last summer"/"Q1"), or ISO ("2026-04-01"). Default: 30d.

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

interval.description:
"none": total consumption for the whole period (default).
"day": daily breakdown. "week": weekly. "month": monthly.
Required when using filter_operator/filter_value.

filter_operator.description:
Filter results to buckets where consumption satisfies [op] filter_value. Requires interval.
E.g. "which days used more than 10 kWh?" → interval="day", filter_operator=">", filter_value=10

filter_value.description: Threshold for filter_operator. Required when filter_operator is set.

max_results.description: Applies to interval breakdown only (not scalar). Default: 100. Pass "all" for complete series. Response shows total count when capped.

comparison.description:
Only applicable with interval="none". Compares the total to a reference period.
"previous_period": equal-length period immediately before.
"same_period_last_year": same calendar dates 1 year ago.
Returns both totals and the absolute/percentage difference.

function.name: ha_history_detect_sessions
function.description:
Detects activity sessions from a numeric sensor using a power/value threshold.
Use for: "How many times was the car charged in February?",
"How many times did the washing machine run last week?",
"What was the longest heating session last month?",
"What time did the last dishwasher run end each night?" (use group_by="day")
Uses long-term hourly statistics → full date range, no retention limit, ±1h precision.
For binary sensors (motion, door) or person/zone state history,
use ha_history_get_state_history instead.
Returns: event count, total duration, compact session list, or daily summary (with group_by="day").

entity.description: Exact entity_id from ha_history_list_entities. Do not guess.

start_time.description: Period start. Formats: relative (7d/30d/24h/2w/1y), named ("last month"/"last week"/"yesterday"/"last summer"/"Q1"), or ISO ("2026-04-01"). Default: 30d. Special: "overnight" = 22:00 yesterday → 06:00 today.

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

threshold.description:
Minimum value to count as "active". Required.
Example: 100 for Watts (EV charger, heater, washing machine).
The sensor must have long-term statistics in Home Assistant.

min_duration_minutes.description:
Minimum session duration in minutes. Filters out sessions shorter than this. Default: 1.
Note: uses hourly statistics, so the minimum meaningful value is 60 min (one hour bucket).
Values below 60 have no additional effect.

max_gap_minutes.description:
Maximum inactivity gap to bridge between two active periods, treating them as
one session. Default: 0 (no merging). Useful for devices with scheduled pauses:
e.g. washing machine with a 1–2h break between cycles (set 90–150).
Note: uses hourly statistics so gaps are in whole hours —
values below 60 have no effect; use multiples of 60 (e.g. 90, 120).

group_by.description:
Group sessions by calendar day. Returns one compact row per day:
  date | session count | first session start | last session end | total active
Use for high-frequency sensors (motion, door) where the session list is too long,
or when daily patterns matter: "when did activity start each morning?",
"how many times per day did the washing machine run?"
For cross-midnight patterns (bedtime, night shifts), combine with day_start_hour=6.
Summary stats (total sessions, active days, avg/day) always cover the full dataset.

day_start_hour.description:
Only with group_by="day". Shifts the day boundary from midnight to a later hour (0–23).
Default: 0 (midnight). Set to 6 for "night" grouping: a day runs 06:00 → next 05:59,
so post-midnight activity (e.g. 01:30) is attributed to the previous evening's date.
Use for: "what time did the last person go to bed each night?",
overnight patterns, night shifts, anything spanning midnight.

max_results.description:
Max rows to return. Default: 20. Pass "all" to list all.
Without group_by: caps individual sessions.
With group_by="day": caps calendar days shown.
Summary stats always cover the full dataset regardless.

comparison.description:
Compare session count and duration to a reference period.
"previous_period": the immediately preceding equal-length period.
"same_period_last_year": the same calendar period 12 months ago.

function.name: ha_history_get_state_history
function.description:
Gets the state-change history for any discrete-state entity in Sanzay.
Use for binary sensors (motion, door, window, presence), person/device_tracker
(zone and location history), and any entity with named states.

Two modes:
  Session mode (state_value provided): detects periods in that state.
    "How many times was the front door open last week?",
    "When did Olivia arrive at LFO this morning?" (entity=person.olivia, state_value="LFO"),
    "Was there any motion in the garage overnight?" (state_value="on"),
    "When was the last time the cat litter was cleaned?" (state_value="cleaning")
  Timeline mode (no state_value): shows all state transitions.
    "Show me Olivia's location history today"
    "Show all door events this morning"

Source: HA recorder state history — limited to ~10 days by default.
Returns: timeline of transitions, or session count/durations (session mode).

entity.description: Exact entity_id. Use ha_history_list_entities to find it. Do not guess.

state_value.description:
Target state to detect sessions for.
Binary sensors: "on" (active) or "off".
Person/device_tracker: zone name e.g. "LFO", "home", "not_home".

start_time.description: Period start. Formats: relative (7d/30d/24h/2w/1y), named ("last month"/"last week"/"yesterday"/"last summer"/"Q1"), or ISO ("2026-04-01"). Default: 30d. Special: "overnight" = 22:00 yesterday → 06:00 today.

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

min_duration_minutes.description:
Session mode only. Minimum duration in minutes to count as a session. Default: 0.
Useful to filter out very brief state changes (e.g. motion sensor glitches).

max_gap_minutes.description:
Session mode only. Bridge brief inactive gaps into one session. Default: 0 (no merging).
Useful for motion sensors where a person pauses for a minute: set 2–5.

group_by.description:
Session mode only. Group sessions by calendar day.
Returns one row per day: date | count | first start | last end | total active.
Combine with day_start_hour=6 for overnight/cross-midnight grouping.

day_start_hour.description:
Only with group_by="day". Shifts the day boundary (0–23). Default: 0 (midnight).
Set to 6 so post-midnight activity (e.g. 01:30) is attributed to the previous evening.
Use for: "what time did the last person arrive home each night?", night patterns.

max_results.description:
Max rows to return. Default: 20. Pass "all" to list all.
Timeline mode: caps transitions shown. Session mode: caps sessions or days.

comparison.description: Session mode only. Compare session count and duration to a reference period.

function.name: ha_history_get_current_time
function.description:
Returns the current date and time from the Home Assistant server (Sanzay).
Call this before making any time-based query when the user uses a relative or named time
expression: "last month", "this winter", "yesterday", "last year", "in april", "recently".
Do not rely on your training data to infer the current date — it will often be wrong.
Skip only if an absolute ISO date range has already been stated in this conversation.

function.name: ha_history_list_entities
function.description:
Lists Sanzay sensors that have historical data available.
Each result includes the entity_id, friendly name, room/area, unit, and sensor type.
Call this to find the correct entity_id before querying any sensor you don't already know.
Skip only if the entity_id was already resolved earlier in this conversation.
Also use for explicit sensor discovery or when a previous call returned an ambiguous match.
Binary sensors (motion, doors, presence) need domain="binary_sensor" — no statistics.
For location tracking use domain="device_tracker". For zones use domain="zone".

domain.description:
Filter by entity domain. Common values:
"sensor" — numeric/measurement sensors (temperature, energy, power).
"binary_sensor" — on/off sensors (motion, doors, windows).
"device_tracker" — person/phone location tracking.
"zone" — geographical zones (home, work, school…).
Leave empty to include all domains with statistics.

search.description:
Search terms matched against entity_id, friendly name, device name, area, device class, and unit.
Multiple space-separated words are treated as OR — an entity matches if ANY word appears in any field.
E.g. "temperature humidity" returns all temperature OR humidity sensors.
E.g. "power energy electricity" returns any entity matching at least one of those words.

include_state.description:
When true, adds the current state value to each result row. Default: false.
Useful when you need both the entity_id and its current value in one call.
For a single entity's full state details, prefer ha_history_get_state instead.

function.name: ha_history_get_state
function.description:
Returns the current state of any Sanzay entity.
Use for: "What is the temperature in the kitchen right now?",
"Is the front door open?", "Where is person X?", "Is the washing machine running?"
Works for all entity domains: sensor, binary_sensor, device_tracker, zone,
climate, switch, light, cover, media_player, etc.
Returns: current state value, unit, last changed time, and key attributes.
Call ha_history_list_entities first if you don't know the exact entity_id.

entity_id.description: Exact entity_id from ha_history_list_entities. Do not guess.

function.name: ha_history_get_sensor_stats
function.description:
Computes statistics for a Sanzay sensor measuring instantaneous values:
temperature, humidity, CO₂, pressure, illuminance, or power draw in Watts.
Use for: "What was the lowest temperature last night?", "Average humidity in April?",
"Warmest day last summer?", "How many days above 25°C?", "Which days had frost?",
"At what time of day is it usually hottest?", "Which day of the week is most humid?"
Do NOT use for energy consumption (kWh) → use ha_history_get_consumption.
Do NOT use for event counting → use ha_history_detect_sessions.

entity.description: Exact entity_id from ha_history_list_entities (e.g. "sensor.ruuvitag_fc8f_temperature"). Do not guess.

start_time.description: Period start. Formats: relative (7d/30d/24h/2w/1y), named ("last month"/"last week"/"yesterday"/"last summer"/"Q1"), or ISO ("2026-04-01"). Default: 30d.

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

aggregation.description:
"mean": average. "min": lowest. "max": highest. "median": middle value.
"count" (requires group_by + filter): counts per slot how many readings satisfied
  the filter condition. Returns "N/M" per slot — e.g. "18/30 days at 06:00 exceeded 21°C".
  Use for: "how many days at each hour exceeded 25°C?",
           "how many weeks on each day-of-week was humidity above 70%?"
Choose: "hottest" → "max", "coldest" → "min", "average/typical" → "mean",
"how many X had Y?" with group_by → "count".

interval.description:
"none": one value for the whole period (default).
"hour"/"day"/"week"/"month": time series — one value per bucket.
Required when using filter_operator/filter_value.
Cannot be used together with group_by.

group_by.description:
Groups all readings by a repeating time unit across the full period, then applies
the aggregation. Ideal for pattern questions:
"hour_of_day": 24 buckets (00:00–23:00) — "at what time of day is it usually hottest?"
"day_of_week": 7 buckets (Mon–Sun) — "which day of the week is most humid?"
Cannot be used with interval. filter_operator/filter_value work normally on top.

filter_operator.description:
Filter results to buckets where the aggregated value satisfies [op] filter_value.
Requires interval (not "none") or group_by. Response includes matching bucket count.
E.g. frost days: aggregation="min", filter_operator="<", filter_value=0

filter_value.description: Threshold for filter_operator. Required when filter_operator is set.

max_results.description: Applies to interval time-series only (not scalar or group_by). Default: 100. Pass "all" for the complete series. Response shows total count when capped.

function.name: ha_history_get_consumption
function.description:
Calculates how much energy, water, gas, or other resource was consumed or produced
in Sanzay over a time period.
Use for: "How much electricity did the car charger use in February?",
"Total electricity last month?", "Solar production last week?",
"Daily energy usage last week", "Compare grid import this April vs last April",
"Which days used more than 10 kWh?"
Always returns consumption (the change over the period), never raw meter readings.
Do NOT use for instantaneous sensors (temperature, power in Watts) → use ha_history_get_sensor_stats.

entity.description: Exact entity_id from ha_history_list_entities (look for type="cumulative"). E.g. "sensor.electricity_meter_kwh". Do not guess.

start_time.description: Period start. Formats: relative (7d/30d/24h/2w/1y), named ("last month"/"last week"/"yesterday"/"last summer"/"Q1"), or ISO ("2026-04-01"). Default: 30d.

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

interval.description:
"none": total consumption for the whole period (default).
"day": daily breakdown. "week": weekly. "month": monthly.
Required when using filter_operator/filter_value.

filter_operator.description:
Filter results to buckets where consumption satisfies [op] filter_value. Requires interval.
E.g. "which days used more than 10 kWh?" → interval="day", filter_operator=">", filter_value=10

filter_value.description: Threshold for filter_operator. Required when filter_operator is set.

max_results.description: Applies to interval breakdown only (not scalar). Default: 100. Pass "all" for complete series. Response shows total count when capped.

comparison.description:
Only applicable with interval="none". Compares the total to a reference period.
"previous_period": equal-length period immediately before.
"same_period_last_year": same calendar dates 1 year ago.
Returns both totals and the absolute/percentage difference.

function.name: ha_history_detect_sessions
function.description:
Detects activity sessions from a numeric sensor using a power/value threshold.
Use for: "How many times was the car charged in February?",
"How many times did the washing machine run last week?",
"What was the longest heating session last month?",
"What time did the last dishwasher run end each night?" (use group_by="day")
Uses long-term hourly statistics → full date range, no retention limit, ±1h precision.
For binary sensors (motion, door) or person/zone state history,
use ha_history_get_state_history instead.
Returns: event count, total duration, compact session list, or daily summary (with group_by="day").

entity.description: Exact entity_id from ha_history_list_entities. Do not guess.

start_time.description: Period start. Formats: relative (7d/30d/24h/2w/1y), named ("last month"/"last week"/"yesterday"/"last summer"/"Q1"), or ISO ("2026-04-01"). Default: 30d. Special: "overnight" = 22:00 yesterday → 06:00 today.

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

threshold.description:
Minimum value to count as "active". Required.
Example: 100 for Watts (EV charger, heater, washing machine).
The sensor must have long-term statistics in Home Assistant.

min_duration_minutes.description:
Minimum session duration in minutes. Filters out sessions shorter than this. Default: 1.
Note: uses hourly statistics, so the minimum meaningful value is 60 min (one hour bucket).
Values below 60 have no additional effect.

max_gap_minutes.description:
Maximum inactivity gap to bridge between two active periods, treating them as
one session. Default: 0 (no merging). Useful for devices with scheduled pauses:
e.g. washing machine with a 1–2h break between cycles (set 90–150).
Note: uses hourly statistics so gaps are in whole hours —
values below 60 have no effect; use multiples of 60 (e.g. 90, 120).

group_by.description:
Group sessions by calendar day. Returns one compact row per day:
  date | session count | first session start | last session end | total active
Use for high-frequency sensors (motion, door) where the session list is too long,
or when daily patterns matter: "when did activity start each morning?",
"how many times per day did the washing machine run?"
For cross-midnight patterns (bedtime, night shifts), combine with day_start_hour=6.
Summary stats (total sessions, active days, avg/day) always cover the full dataset.

day_start_hour.description:
Only with group_by="day". Shifts the day boundary from midnight to a later hour (0–23).
Default: 0 (midnight). Set to 6 for "night" grouping: a day runs 06:00 → next 05:59,
so post-midnight activity (e.g. 01:30) is attributed to the previous evening's date.
Use for: "what time did the last person go to bed each night?",
overnight patterns, night shifts, anything spanning midnight.

max_results.description:
Max rows to return. Default: 20. Pass "all" to list all.
Without group_by: caps individual sessions.
With group_by="day": caps calendar days shown.
Summary stats always cover the full dataset regardless.

comparison.description:
Compare session count and duration to a reference period.
"previous_period": the immediately preceding equal-length period.
"same_period_last_year": the same calendar period 12 months ago.

function.name: ha_history_get_state_history
function.description:
Gets the state-change history for any discrete-state entity in Sanzay.
Use for binary sensors (motion, door, window, presence), person/device_tracker
(zone and location history), and any entity with named states.

Two modes:
  Session mode (state_value provided): detects periods in that state.
    "How many times was the front door open last week?",
    "When did Olivia arrive at LFO this morning?" (entity=person.olivia, state_value="LFO"),
    "Was there any motion in the garage overnight?" (state_value="on"),
    "When was the last time the cat litter was cleaned?" (state_value="cleaning")
  Timeline mode (no state_value): shows all state transitions.
    "Show me Olivia's location history today"
    "Show all door events this morning"

Source: HA recorder state history — limited to ~10 days by default.
Returns: timeline of transitions, or session count/durations (session mode).

entity.description: Exact entity_id. Use ha_history_list_entities to find it. Do not guess.

state_value.description:
Target state to detect sessions for.
Binary sensors: "on" (active) or "off".
Person/device_tracker: zone name e.g. "LFO", "home", "not_home".
Matching is case-insensitive.
Omit to get a full timeline of all state transitions instead.

start_time.description: Period start. Formats: relative (7d/30d/24h/2w/1y), named ("last month"/"last week"/"yesterday"/"last summer"/"Q1"), or ISO ("2026-04-01"). Default: 30d. Special: "overnight" = 22:00 yesterday → 06:00 today.

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

min_duration_minutes.description:
Session mode only. Minimum duration in minutes to count as a session. Default: 0.
Useful to filter out very brief state changes (e.g. motion sensor glitches).

max_gap_minutes.description:
Session mode only. Bridge brief inactive gaps into one session. Default: 0 (no merging).
Useful for motion sensors where a person pauses for a minute: set 2–5.

group_by.description:
Session mode only. Group sessions by calendar day.
Returns one row per day: date | count | first start | last end | total active.
Combine with day_start_hour=6 for overnight/cross-midnight grouping.

day_start_hour.description:
Only with group_by="day". Shifts the day boundary (0–23). Default: 0 (midnight).
Set to 6 so post-midnight activity (e.g. 01:30) is attributed to the previous evening.
Use for: "what time did the last person arrive home each night?", night patterns.

max_results.description:
Max rows to return. Default: 20. Pass "all" to list all.
Timeline mode: caps transitions shown. Session mode: caps sessions or days.

comparison.description: Session mode only. Compare session count and duration to a reference period.

function.name: ha_history_get_current_time
function.description:
Returns the current date and time from the Home Assistant server (Sanzay).
Call this before making any time-based query when the user uses a relative or named time
expression: "last month", "this winter", "yesterday", "last year", "in april", "recently".
Do not rely on your training data to infer the current date — it will often be wrong.
Skip only if an absolute ISO date range has already been stated in this conversation.

function.name: ha_history_list_entities
function.description:
Lists Sanzay sensors that have historical data available.
Each result includes the entity_id, friendly name, room/area, unit, and sensor type.
Call this to find the correct entity_id before querying any sensor you don't already know.
Skip only if the entity_id was already resolved earlier in this conversation.
Also use for explicit sensor discovery or when a previous call returned an ambiguous match.
Binary sensors (motion, doors, presence) need domain="binary_sensor" — no statistics.
For location tracking use domain="device_tracker". For zones use domain="zone".

domain.description:
Filter by entity domain. Common values:
"sensor" — numeric/measurement sensors (temperature, energy, power).
"binary_sensor" — on/off sensors (motion, doors, windows).
"device_tracker" — person/phone location tracking.
"zone" — geographical zones (home, work, school…).
Leave empty to include all domains with statistics.

search.description:
Search terms matched against entity_id, friendly name, device name, area, device class, and unit.
Multiple space-separated words are treated as OR — an entity matches if ANY word appears in any field.
E.g. "temperature humidity" returns all temperature OR humidity sensors.
E.g. "power energy electricity" returns any entity matching at least one of those words.

include_state.description:
When true, adds the current state value to each result row. Default: false.
Useful when you need both the entity_id and its current value in one call.
For a single entity's full state details, prefer ha_history_get_state instead.

function.name: ha_history_get_state
function.description:
Returns the current state of any Sanzay entity.
Use for: "What is the temperature in the kitchen right now?",
"Is the front door open?", "Where is person X?", "Is the washing machine running?"
Works for all entity domains: sensor, binary_sensor, device_tracker, zone,
climate, switch, light, cover, media_player, etc.
Returns: current state value, unit, last changed time, and key attributes.
Call ha_history_list_entities first if you don't know the exact entity_id.

entity_id.description: Exact entity_id from ha_history_list_entities. Do not guess.

function.name: ha_history_get_sensor_stats
function.description:
Computes statistics for a Sanzay sensor measuring instantaneous values:
temperature, humidity, CO₂, pressure, illuminance, or power draw in Watts.
Use for: "What was the lowest temperature last night?", "Average humidity in April?",
"Warmest day last summer?", "How many days above 25°C?", "Which days had frost?",
"At what time of day is it usually hottest?", "Which day of the week is most humid?"
Do NOT use for energy consumption (kWh) → use ha_history_get_consumption.
Do NOT use for event counting → use ha_history_detect_sessions.

entity.description: Exact entity_id from ha_history_list_entities (e.g. "sensor.ruuvitag_fc8f_temperature"). Do not guess.

start_time.description: Period start. Formats: relative (7d/30d/24h/2w/1y), named ("last month"/"last week"/"yesterday"/"last summer"/"Q1"), or ISO ("2026-04-01"). Default: 30d.

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

aggregation.description:
"mean": average. "min": lowest. "max": highest. "median": middle value.
"count" (requires group_by + filter): counts per slot how many readings satisfied
  the filter condition. Returns "N/M" per slot — e.g. "18/30 days at 06:00 exceeded 21°C".
  Use for: "how many days at each hour exceeded 25°C?",
           "how many weeks on each day-of-week was humidity above 70%?"
Choose: "hottest" → "max", "coldest" → "min", "average/typical" → "mean",
"how many X had Y?" with group_by → "count".

interval.description:
"none": one value for the whole period (default).
"hour"/"day"/"week"/"month": time series — one value per bucket.
Required when using filter_operator/filter_value.
Cannot be used together with group_by.

group_by.description:
Groups all readings by a repeating time unit across the full period, then applies
the aggregation. Ideal for pattern questions:
"hour_of_day": 24 buckets (00:00–23:00) — "at what time of day is it usually hottest?"
"day_of_week": 7 buckets (Mon–Sun) — "which day of the week is most humid?"
Cannot be used with interval. filter_operator/filter_value work normally on top.

filter_operator.description:
Filter results to buckets where the aggregated value satisfies [op] filter_value.
Requires interval (not "none") or group_by. Response includes matching bucket count.
E.g. frost days: aggregation="min", filter_operator="<", filter_value=0

filter_value.description: Threshold for filter_operator. Required when filter_operator is set.

max_results.description: Applies to interval time-series only (not scalar or group_by). Default: 100. Pass "all" for the complete series. Response shows total count when capped.

function.name: ha_history_get_consumption
function.description:
Calculates how much energy, water, gas, or other resource was consumed or produced
in Sanzay over a time period.
Use for: "How much electricity did the car charger use in February?",
"Total electricity last month?", "Solar production last week?",
"Daily energy usage last week", "Compare grid import this April vs last April",
"Which days used more than 10 kWh?"
Always returns consumption (the change over the period), never raw meter readings.
Do NOT use for instantaneous sensors (temperature, power in Watts) → use ha_history_get_sensor_stats.

entity.description: Exact entity_id from ha_history_list_entities (look for type="cumulative"). E.g. "sensor.electricity_meter_kwh". Do not guess.

start_time.description: Period start. Formats: relative (7d/30d/24h/2w/1y), named ("last month"/"last week"/"yesterday"/"last summer"/"Q1"), or ISO ("2026-04-01"). Default: 30d.

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

interval.description:
"none": total consumption for the whole period (default).
"day": daily breakdown. "week": weekly. "month": monthly.
Required when using filter_operator/filter_value.

filter_operator.description:
Filter results to buckets where consumption satisfies [op] filter_value. Requires interval.
E.g. "which days used more than 10 kWh?" → interval="day", filter_operator=">", filter_value=10

filter_value.description: Threshold for filter_operator. Required when filter_operator is set.

max_results.description: Applies to interval breakdown only (not scalar). Default: 100. Pass "all" for complete series. Response shows total count when capped.

comparison.description:
Only applicable with interval="none". Compares the total to a reference period.
"previous_period": equal-length period immediately before.
"same_period_last_year": same calendar dates 1 year ago.
Returns both totals and the absolute/percentage difference.

function.name: ha_history_detect_sessions
function.description:
Detects activity sessions from a numeric sensor using a power/value threshold.
Use for: "How many times was the car charged in February?",
"How many times did the washing machine run last week?",
"What was the longest heating session last month?",
"What time did the last dishwasher run end each night?" (use group_by="day")
Uses long-term hourly statistics → full date range, no retention limit, ±1h precision.
For binary sensors (motion, door) or person/zone state history,
use ha_history_get_state_history instead.
Returns: event count, total duration, compact session list, or daily summary (with group_by="day").

entity.description: Exact entity_id from ha_history_list_entities. Do not guess.

start_time.description: Period start. Formats: relative (7d/30d/24h/2w/1y), named ("last month"/"last week"/"yesterday"/"last summer"/"Q1"), or ISO ("2026-04-01"). Default: 30d. Special: "overnight" = 22:00 yesterday → 06:00 today.

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

threshold.description:
Minimum value to count as "active". Required.
Example: 100 for Watts (EV charger, heater, washing machine).
The sensor must have long-term statistics in Home Assistant.

min_duration_minutes.description:
Minimum session duration in minutes. Filters out sessions shorter than this. Default: 1.
Note: uses hourly statistics, so the minimum meaningful value is 60 min (one hour bucket).
Values below 60 have no additional effect.

max_gap_minutes.description:
Maximum inactivity gap to bridge between two active periods, treating them as
one session. Default: 0 (no merging). Useful for devices with scheduled pauses:
e.g. washing machine with a 1–2h break between cycles (set 90–150).
Note: uses hourly statistics so gaps are in whole hours —
values below 60 have no effect; use multiples of 60 (e.g. 90, 120).

group_by.description:
Group sessions by calendar day. Returns one compact row per day:
  date | session count | first session start | last session end | total active
Use for high-frequency sensors (motion, door) where the session list is too long,
or when daily patterns matter: "when did activity start each morning?",
"how many times per day did the washing machine run?"
For cross-midnight patterns (bedtime, night shifts), combine with day_start_hour=6.
Summary stats (total sessions, active days, avg/day) always cover the full dataset.

day_start_hour.description:
Only with group_by="day". Shifts the day boundary from midnight to a later hour (0–23).
Default: 0 (midnight). Set to 6 for "night" grouping: a day runs 06:00 → next 05:59,
so post-midnight activity (e.g. 01:30) is attributed to the previous evening's date.
Use for: "what time did the last person go to bed each night?",
overnight patterns, night shifts, anything spanning midnight.

max_results.description:
Max rows to return. Default: 20. Pass "all" to list all.
Without group_by: caps individual sessions.
With group_by="day": caps calendar days shown.
Summary stats always cover the full dataset regardless.

comparison.description:
Compare session count and duration to a reference period.
"previous_period": the immediately preceding equal-length period.
"same_period_last_year": the same calendar period 12 months ago.

function.name: ha_history_get_state_history
function.description:
Gets the state-change history for any discrete-state entity in Sanzay.
Use for binary sensors (motion, door, window, presence), person/device_tracker
(zone and location history), and any entity with named states.

Two modes:
  Session mode (state_value provided): detects periods in that state.
    "How many times was the front door open last week?",
    "When did Olivia arrive at LFO this morning?" (entity=person.olivia, state_value="LFO"),
    "Was there any motion in the garage overnight?" (state_value="on"),
    "When was the last time the cat litter was cleaned?" (state_value="cleaning")
  Timeline mode (no state_value): shows all state transitions.
    "Show me Olivia's location history today"
    "Show all door events this morning"

Source: HA recorder state history — limited to ~10 days by default.
Returns: timeline of transitions, or session count/durations (session mode).

entity.description: Exact entity_id. Use ha_history_list_entities to find it. Do not guess.

state_value.description:
Target state to detect sessions for.
Binary sensors: "on" (active) or "off".
Person/device_tracker: zone name e.g. "LFO", "home", "not_home".
Matching is case-insensitive.
Omit to get a full timeline of all state transitions instead.

start_time.description: Period start. Formats: relative (7d/30d/24h/2w/1y), named ("last month"/"last week"/"yesterday"/"last summer"/"Q1"), or ISO ("2026-04-01"). Default: 30d. Special: "overnight" = 22:00 yesterday → 06:00 today.

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

min_duration_minutes.description:
Session mode only. Minimum duration in minutes to count as a session. Default: 0.
Useful to filter out very brief state changes (e.g. motion sensor glitches).

max_gap_minutes.description:
Session mode only. Bridge brief inactive gaps into one session. Default: 0 (no merging).
Useful for motion sensors where a person pauses for a minute: set 2–5.

group_by.description:
Session mode only. Group sessions by calendar day.
Returns one row per day: date | count | first start | last end | total active.
Combine with day_start_hour=6 for overnight/cross-midnight grouping.

day_start_hour.description:
Only with group_by="day". Shifts the day boundary (0–23). Default: 0 (midnight).
Set to 6 so post-midnight activity (e.g. 01:30) is attributed to the previous evening.
Use for: "what time did the last person arrive home each night?", night patterns.

max_results.description:
Max rows to return. Default: 20. Pass "all" to list all.
Timeline mode: caps transitions shown. Session mode: caps sessions or days.

comparison.description: Session mode only. Compare session count and duration to a reference period.

function.name: ha_history_get_current_time
function.description:
Returns the current date and time from the Home Assistant server (Sanzay).
Call this before making any time-based query when the user uses a relative or named time
expression: "last month", "this winter", "yesterday", "last year", "in april", "recently".
Do not rely on your training data to infer the current date — it will often be wrong.
Skip only if an absolute ISO date range has already been stated in this conversation.

function.name: ha_history_list_entities
function.description:
Lists Sanzay sensors that have historical data available.
Each result includes the entity_id, friendly name, room/area, unit, and sensor type.
Call this to find the correct entity_id before querying any sensor you don't already know.
Skip only if the entity_id was already resolved earlier in this conversation.
Also use for explicit sensor discovery or when a previous call returned an ambiguous match.
Binary sensors (motion, doors, presence) need domain="binary_sensor" — no statistics.
For location tracking use domain="device_tracker". For zones use domain="zone".

domain.description:
Filter by entity domain. Common values:
"sensor" — numeric/measurement sensors (temperature, energy, power).
"binary_sensor" — on/off sensors (motion, doors, windows).
"device_tracker" — person/phone location tracking.
"zone" — geographical zones (home, work, school…).
Leave empty to include all domains with statistics.

search.description:
Search terms matched against entity_id, friendly name, device name, area, device class, and unit.
Multiple space-separated words are treated as OR — an entity matches if ANY word appears in any field.
E.g. "temperature humidity" returns all temperature OR humidity sensors.
E.g. "power energy electricity" returns any entity matching at least one of those words.

include_state.description:
When true, adds the current state value to each result row. Default: false.
Useful when you need both the entity_id and its current value in one call.
For a single entity's full state details, prefer ha_history_get_state instead.

function.name: ha_history_get_state
function.description:
Returns the current state of any Sanzay entity.
Use for: "What is the temperature in the kitchen right now?",
"Is the front door open?", "Where is person X?", "Is the washing machine running?"
Works for all entity domains: sensor, binary_sensor, device_tracker, zone,
climate, switch, light, cover, media_player, etc.
Returns: current state value, unit, last changed time, and key attributes.
Call ha_history_list_entities first if you don't know the exact entity_id.

entity_id.description: Exact entity_id from ha_history_list_entities. Do not guess.

function.name: ha_history_get_sensor_stats
function.description:
Computes statistics for a Sanzay sensor measuring instantaneous values:
temperature, humidity, CO₂, pressure, illuminance, or power draw in Watts.
Use for: "What was the lowest temperature last night?", "Average humidity in April?",
"Warmest day last summer?", "How many days above 25°C?", "Which days had frost?",
"At what time of day is it usually hottest?", "Which day of the week is most humid?"
Do NOT use for energy consumption (kWh) → use ha_history_get_consumption.
Do NOT use for event counting → use ha_history_detect_sessions.

entity.description: Exact entity_id from ha_history_list_entities (e.g. "sensor.ruuvitag_fc8f_temperature"). Do not guess.

start_time.description: Period start. Formats: relative (7d/30d/24h/2w/1y), named ("last month"/"last week"/"yesterday"/"last summer"/"Q1"), or ISO ("2026-04-01"). Default: 30d.

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

aggregation.description:
"mean": average. "min": lowest. "max": highest. "median": middle value.
"count" (requires group_by + filter): counts per slot how many readings satisfied
  the filter condition. Returns "N/M" per slot — e.g. "18/30 days at 06:00 exceeded 21°C".
  Use for: "how many days at each hour exceeded 25°C?",
           "how many weeks on each day-of-week was humidity above 70%?"
Choose: "hottest" → "max", "coldest" → "min", "average/typical" → "mean",
"how many X had Y?" with group_by → "count".

interval.description:
"none": one value for the whole period (default).
"hour"/"day"/"week"/"month": time series — one value per bucket.
Required when using filter_operator/filter_value.
Cannot be used together with group_by.

group_by.description:
Groups all readings by a repeating time unit across the full period, then applies
the aggregation. Ideal for pattern questions:
"hour_of_day": 24 buckets (00:00–23:00) — "at what time of day is it usually hottest?"
"day_of_week": 7 buckets (Mon–Sun) — "which day of the week is most humid?"
Cannot be used with interval. filter_operator/filter_value work normally on top.

filter_operator.description:
Filter results to buckets where the aggregated value satisfies [op] filter_value.
Requires interval (not "none") or group_by. Response includes matching bucket count.
E.g. frost days: aggregation="min", filter_operator="<", filter_value=0

filter_value.description: Threshold for filter_operator. Required when filter_operator is set.

max_results.description: Applies to interval time-series only (not scalar or group_by). Default: 100. Pass "all" for the complete series. Response shows total count when capped.

function.name: ha_history_get_consumption
function.description:
Calculates how much energy, water, gas, or other resource was consumed or produced
in Sanzay over a time period.
Use for: "How much electricity did the car charger use in February?",
"Total electricity last month?", "Solar production last week?",
"Daily energy usage last week", "Compare grid import this April vs last April",
"Which days used more than 10 kWh?"
Always returns consumption (the change over the period), never raw meter readings.
Do NOT use for instantaneous sensors (temperature, power in Watts) → use ha_history_get_sensor_stats.

entity.description: Exact entity_id from ha_history_list_entities (look for type="cumulative"). E.g. "sensor.electricity_meter_kwh". Do not guess.

start_time.description: Period start. Formats: relative (7d/30d/24h/2w/1y), named ("last month"/"last week"/"yesterday"/"last summer"/"Q1"), or ISO ("2026-04-01"). Default: 30d.

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

interval.description:
"none": total consumption for the whole period (default).
"day": daily breakdown. "week": weekly. "month": monthly.
Required when using filter_operator/filter_value.

filter_operator.description:
Filter results to buckets where consumption satisfies [op] filter_value. Requires interval.
E.g. "which days used more than 10 kWh?" → interval="day", filter_operator=">", filter_value=10

filter_value.description: Threshold for filter_operator. Required when filter_operator is set.

max_results.description: Applies to interval breakdown only (not scalar). Default: 100. Pass "all" for complete series. Response shows total count when capped.

comparison.description:
Only applicable with interval="none". Compares the total to a reference period.
"previous_period": equal-length period immediately before.
"same_period_last_year": same calendar dates 1 year ago.
Returns both totals and the absolute/percentage difference.

function.name: ha_history_detect_sessions
function.description:
Detects activity sessions from a numeric sensor using a power/value threshold.
Use for: "How many times was the car charged in February?",
"How many times did the washing machine run last week?",
"What was the longest heating session last month?",
"What time did the last dishwasher run end each night?" (use group_by="day")
Uses long-term hourly statistics → full date range, no retention limit, ±1h precision.
For binary sensors (motion, door) or person/zone state history,
use ha_history_get_state_history instead.
Returns: event count, total duration, compact session list, or daily summary (with group_by="day").

entity.description: Exact entity_id from ha_history_list_entities. Do not guess.

start_time.description: Period start. Formats: relative (7d/30d/24h/2w/1y), named ("last month"/"last week"/"yesterday"/"last summer"/"Q1"), or ISO ("2026-04-01"). Default: 30d. Special: "overnight" = 22:00 yesterday → 06:00 today.

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

threshold.description:
Minimum value to count as "active". Required.
Example: 100 for Watts (EV charger, heater, washing machine).
The sensor must have long-term statistics in Home Assistant.

min_duration_minutes.description:
Minimum session duration in minutes. Filters out sessions shorter than this. Default: 1.
Note: uses hourly statistics, so the minimum meaningful value is 60 min (one hour bucket).
Values below 60 have no additional effect.

max_gap_minutes.description:
Maximum inactivity gap to bridge between two active periods, treating them as
one session. Default: 0 (no merging). Useful for devices with scheduled pauses:
e.g. washing machine with a 1–2h break between cycles (set 90–150).
Note: uses hourly statistics so gaps are in whole hours —
values below 60 have no effect; use multiples of 60 (e.g. 90, 120).

group_by.description:
Group sessions by calendar day. Returns one compact row per day:
  date | session count | first session start | last session end | total active
Use for high-frequency sensors (motion, door) where the session list is too long,
or when daily patterns matter: "when did activity start each morning?",
"how many times per day did the washing machine run?"
For cross-midnight patterns (bedtime, night shifts), combine with day_start_hour=6.
Summary stats (total sessions, active days, avg/day) always cover the full dataset.

day_start_hour.description:
Only with group_by="day". Shifts the day boundary from midnight to a later hour (0–23).
Default: 0 (midnight). Set to 6 for "night" grouping: a day runs 06:00 → next 05:59,
so post-midnight activity (e.g. 01:30) is attributed to the previous evening's date.
Use for: "what time did the last person go to bed each night?",
overnight patterns, night shifts, anything spanning midnight.

max_results.description:
Max rows to return. Default: 20. Pass "all" to list all.
Without group_by: caps individual sessions.
With group_by="day": caps calendar days shown.
Summary stats always cover the full dataset regardless.

comparison.description:
Compare session count and duration to a reference period.
"previous_period": the immediately preceding equal-length period.
"same_period_last_year": the same calendar period 12 months ago.

function.name: ha_history_get_state_history
function.description:
Gets the state-change history for any discrete-state entity in Sanzay.
Use for binary sensors (motion, door, window, presence), person/device_tracker
(zone and location history), and any entity with named states.

Two modes:
  Session mode (state_value provided): detects periods in that state.
    "How many times was the front door open last week?",
    "When did Olivia arrive at LFO this morning?" (entity=person.olivia, state_value="LFO"),
    "Was there any motion in the garage overnight?" (state_value="on"),
    "When was the last time the cat litter was cleaned?" (state_value="cleaning")
  Timeline mode (no state_value): shows all state transitions.
    "Show me Olivia's location history today"
    "Show all door events this morning"

Source: HA recorder state history — limited to ~10 days by default.
Returns: timeline of transitions, or session count/durations (session mode).

entity.description: Exact entity_id. Use ha_history_list_entities to find it. Do not guess.

state_value.description:
Target state to detect sessions for.
Binary sensors: "on" (active) or "off".
Person/device_tracker: zone name e.g. "LFO", "home", "not_home".
Matching is case-insensitive.
Omit to get a full timeline of all state transitions instead.

start_time.description: Period start. Formats: relative (7d/30d/24h/2w/1y), named ("last month"/"last week"/"yesterday"/"last summer"/"Q1"), or ISO ("2026-04-01"). Default: 30d. Special: "overnight" = 22:00 yesterday → 06:00 today.

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

min_duration_minutes.description:
Session mode only. Minimum duration in minutes to count as a session. Default: 0.
Useful to filter out very brief state changes (e.g. motion sensor glitches).

max_gap_minutes.description:
Session mode only. Bridge brief inactive gaps into one session. Default: 0 (no merging).
Useful for motion sensors where a person pauses for a minute: set 2–5.

group_by.description:
Session mode only. Group sessions by calendar day.
Returns one row per day: date | count | first start | last end | total active.
Combine with day_start_hour=6 for overnight/cross-midnight grouping.

day_start_hour.description:
Only with group_by="day". Shifts the day boundary (0–23). Default: 0 (midnight).
Set to 6 so post-midnight activity (e.g. 01:30) is attributed to the previous evening.
Use for: "what time did the last person arrive home each night?", night patterns.

max_results.description:
Max rows to return. Default: 20. Pass "all" to list all.
Timeline mode: caps transitions shown. Session mode: caps sessions or days.

comparison.description: Session mode only. Compare session count and duration to a reference period.

function.description:
Returns the current date and time from the Home Assistant server (Sanzay).
Call this before making any time-based query when the user uses a relative or named time
expression: "last month", "this winter", "yesterday", "last year", "in april", "recently".
Do not rely on your training data to infer the current date — it will often be wrong.
Skip only if an absolute ISO date range has already been stated in this conversation.

function.name: ha_history_list_entities
function.description:
Lists Sanzay sensors that have historical data available.
Each result includes the entity_id, friendly name, room/area, unit, and sensor type.
Call this to find the correct entity_id before querying any sensor you don't already know.
Skip only if the entity_id was already resolved earlier in this conversation.
Also use for explicit sensor discovery or when a previous call returned an ambiguous match.
Binary sensors (motion, doors, presence) need domain="binary_sensor" — no statistics.
For location tracking use domain="device_tracker". For zones use domain="zone".

domain.description:
Filter by entity domain. Common values:
"sensor" — numeric/measurement sensors (temperature, energy, power).
"binary_sensor" — on/off sensors (motion, doors, windows).
"device_tracker" — person/phone location tracking.
"zone" — geographical zones (home, work, school…).
Leave empty to include all domains with statistics.

search.description:
Search terms matched against entity_id, friendly name, device name, area, device class, and unit.
Multiple space-separated words are treated as OR — an entity matches if ANY word appears in any field.
E.g. "temperature humidity" returns all temperature OR humidity sensors.
E.g. "power energy electricity" returns any entity matching at least one of those words.

include_state.description:
When true, adds the current state value to each result row. Default: false.
Useful when you need both the entity_id and its current value in one call.
For a single entity's full state details, prefer ha_history_get_state instead.

function.name: ha_history_get_state
function.description:
Returns the current state of any Sanzay entity.
Use for: "What is the temperature in the kitchen right now?",
"Is the front door open?", "Where is person X?", "Is the washing machine running?"
Works for all entity domains: sensor, binary_sensor, device_tracker, zone,
climate, switch, light, cover, media_player, etc.
Returns: current state value, unit, last changed time, and key attributes.
Call ha_history_list_entities first if you don't know the exact entity_id.

entity_id.description: Exact entity_id from ha_history_list_entities. Do not guess.

function.name: ha_history_get_sensor_stats
function.description:
Computes statistics for a Sanzay sensor measuring instantaneous values:
temperature, humidity, CO₂, pressure, illuminance, or power draw in Watts.
Use for: "What was the lowest temperature last night?", "Average humidity in April?",
"Warmest day last summer?", "How many days above 25°C?", "Which days had frost?",
"At what time of day is it usually hottest?", "Which day of the week is most humid?"
Do NOT use for energy consumption (kWh) → use ha_history_get_consumption.
Do NOT use for event counting → use ha_history_detect_sessions.

entity.description: Exact entity_id from ha_history_list_entities (e.g. "sensor.ruuvitag_fc8f_temperature"). Do not guess.

start_time.description: Period start. Formats: relative (7d/30d/24h/2w/1y), named ("last month"/"last week"/"yesterday"/"last summer"/"Q1"), or ISO ("2026-04-01"). Default: 30d.

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

aggregation.description:
"mean": average. "min": lowest. "max": highest. "median": middle value.
"count" (requires group_by + filter): counts per slot how many readings satisfied
  the filter condition. Returns "N/M" per slot — e.g. "18/30 days at 06:00 exceeded 21°C".
  Use for: "how many days at each hour exceeded 25°C?",
           "how many weeks on each day-of-week was humidity above 70%?"
Choose: "hottest" → "max", "coldest" → "min", "average/typical" → "mean",
"how many X had Y?" with group_by → "count".

interval.description:
"none": one value for the whole period (default).
"hour"/"day"/"week"/"month": time series — one value per bucket.
Required when using filter_operator/filter_value.
Cannot be used together with group_by.

group_by.description:
Groups all readings by a repeating time unit across the full period, then applies
the aggregation. Ideal for pattern questions:
"hour_of_day": 24 buckets (00:00–23:00) — "at what time of day is it usually hottest?"
"day_of_week": 7 buckets (Mon–Sun) — "which day of the week is most humid?"
Cannot be used with interval. filter_operator/filter_value work normally on top.

filter_operator.description:
Filter results to buckets where the aggregated value satisfies [op] filter_value.
Requires interval (not "none") or group_by. Response includes matching bucket count.
E.g. frost days: aggregation="min", filter_operator="<", filter_value=0

filter_value.description: Threshold for filter_operator. Required when filter_operator is set.

max_results.description: Applies to interval time-series only (not scalar or group_by). Default: 100. Pass "all" for the complete series. Response shows total count when capped.

function.name: ha_history_get_consumption
function.description:
Calculates how much energy, water, gas, or other resource was consumed or produced
in Sanzay over a time period.
Use for: "How much electricity did the car charger use in February?",
"Total electricity last month?", "Solar production last week?",
"Daily energy usage last week", "Compare grid import this April vs last April",
"Which days used more than 10 kWh?"
Always returns consumption (the change over the period), never raw meter readings.
Do NOT use for instantaneous sensors (temperature, power in Watts) → use ha_history_get_sensor_stats.

entity.description: Exact entity_id from ha_history_list_entities (look for type="cumulative"). E.g. "sensor.electricity_meter_kwh". Do not guess.

start_time.description: Period start. Formats: relative (7d/30d/24h/2w/1y), named ("last month"/"last week"/"yesterday"/"last summer"/"Q1"), or ISO ("2026-04-01"). Default: 30d.

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

interval.description:
"none": total consumption for the whole period (default).
"day": daily breakdown. "week": weekly. "month": monthly.
Required when using filter_operator/filter_value.

filter_operator.description:
Filter results to buckets where consumption satisfies [op] filter_value. Requires interval.
E.g. "which days used more than 10 kWh?" → interval="day", filter_operator=">", filter_value=10

filter_value.description: Threshold for filter_operator. Required when filter_operator is set.

max_results.description: Applies to interval breakdown only (not scalar). Default: 100. Pass "all" for complete series. Response shows total count when capped.

comparison.description:
Only applicable with interval="none". Compares the total to a reference period.
"previous_period": equal-length period immediately before.
"same_period_last_year": same calendar dates 1 year ago.
Returns both totals and the absolute/percentage difference.

function.name: ha_history_detect_sessions
function.description:
Detects activity sessions from a numeric sensor using a power/value threshold.
Use for: "How many times was the car charged in February?",
"How many times did the washing machine run last week?",
"What was the longest heating session last month?",
"What time did the last dishwasher run end each night?" (use group_by="day")
Uses long-term hourly statistics → full date range, no retention limit, ±1h precision.
For binary sensors (motion, door) or person/zone state history,
use ha_history_get_state_history instead.
Returns: event count, total duration, compact session list, or daily summary (with group_by="day").

entity.description: Exact entity_id from ha_history_list_entities. Do not guess.

start_time.description: Period start. Formats: relative (7d/30d/24h/2w/1y), named ("last month"/"last week"/"yesterday"/"last summer"/"Q1"), or ISO ("2026-04-01"). Default: 30d. Special: "overnight" = 22:00 yesterday → 06:00 today.

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

threshold.description:
Minimum value to count as "active". Required.
Example: 100 for Watts (EV charger, heater, washing machine).
The sensor must have long-term statistics in Home Assistant.

min_duration_minutes.description:
Minimum session duration in minutes. Filters out sessions shorter than this. Default: 1.
Note: uses hourly statistics, so the minimum meaningful value is 60 min (one hour bucket).
Values below 60 have no additional effect.

max_gap_minutes.description:
Maximum inactivity gap to bridge between two active periods, treating them as
one session. Default: 0 (no merging). Useful for devices with scheduled pauses:
e.g. washing machine with a 1–2h break between cycles (set 90–150).
Note: uses hourly statistics so gaps are in whole hours —
values below 60 have no effect; use multiples of 60 (e.g. 90, 120).

group_by.description:
Group sessions by calendar day. Returns one compact row per day:
  date | session count | first session start | last session end | total active
Use for high-frequency sensors (motion, door) where the session list is too long,
or when daily patterns matter: "when did activity start each morning?",
"how many times per day did the washing machine run?"
For cross-midnight patterns (bedtime, night shifts), combine with day_start_hour=6.
Summary stats (total sessions, active days, avg/day) always cover the full dataset.

day_start_hour.description:
Only with group_by="day". Shifts the day boundary from midnight to a later hour (0–23).
Default: 0 (midnight). Set to 6 for "night" grouping: a day runs 06:00 → next 05:59,
so post-midnight activity (e.g. 01:30) is attributed to the previous evening's date.
Use for: "what time did the last person go to bed each night?",
overnight patterns, night shifts, anything spanning midnight.

max_results.description:
Max rows to return. Default: 20. Pass "all" to list all.
Without group_by: caps individual sessions.
With group_by="day": caps calendar days shown.
Summary stats always cover the full dataset regardless.

comparison.description:
Compare session count and duration to a reference period.
"previous_period": the immediately preceding equal-length period.
"same_period_last_year": the same calendar period 12 months ago.

function.name: ha_history_get_state_history
function.description:
Gets the state-change history for any discrete-state entity in Sanzay.
Use for binary sensors (motion, door, window, presence), person/device_tracker
(zone and location history), and any entity with named states.

Two modes:
  Session mode (state_value provided): detects periods in that state.
    "How many times was the front door open last week?",
    "When did Olivia arrive at LFO this morning?" (entity=person.olivia, state_value="LFO"),
    "Was there any motion in the garage overnight?" (state_value="on"),
    "When was the last time the cat litter was cleaned?" (state_value="cleaning")
  Timeline mode (no state_value): shows all state transitions.
    "Show me Olivia's location history today"
    "Show all door events this morning"

Source: HA recorder state history — limited to ~10 days by default.
Returns: timeline of transitions, or session count/durations (session mode).

entity.description: Exact entity_id. Use ha_history_list_entities to find it. Do not guess.

state_value.description:
Target state to detect sessions for.
Binary sensors: "on" (active) or "off".
Person/device_tracker: zone name e.g. "LFO", "home", "not_home".
Matching is case-insensitive.
Omit to get a full timeline of all state transitions instead.

start_time.description: Period start. Formats: relative (7d/30d/24h/2w/1y), named ("last month"/"last week"/"yesterday"/"last summer"/"Q1"), or ISO ("2026-04-01"). Default: 30d. Special: "overnight" = 22:00 yesterday → 06:00 today.

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

min_duration_minutes.description:
Session mode only. Minimum duration in minutes to count as a session. Default: 0.
Useful to filter out very brief state changes (e.g. motion sensor glitches).

max_gap_minutes.description:
Session mode only. Bridge brief inactive gaps into one session. Default: 0 (no merging).
Useful for motion sensors where a person pauses for a minute: set 2–5.

group_by.description:
Session mode only. Group sessions by calendar day.
Returns one row per day: date | count | first start | last end | total active.
Combine with day_start_hour=6 for overnight/cross-midnight grouping.

day_start_hour.description:
Only with group_by="day". Shifts the day boundary (0–23). Default: 0 (midnight).
Set to 6 so post-midnight activity (e.g. 01:30) is attributed to the previous evening.
Use for: "what time did the last person arrive home each night?", night patterns.

max_results.description:
Max rows to return. Default: 20. Pass "all" to list all.
Timeline mode: caps transitions shown. Session mode: caps sessions or days.

comparison.description: Session mode only. Compare session count and duration to a reference period.

- Always state what was measured: which sensor, what period, and what aggregation.

json.name: ha_history_get_consumption
json.description:
Calculates how much energy, water, gas, or other resource was consumed or produced
in Sanzay over a time period.
Use for: "How much electricity did the car charger use in February?",
"Total electricity last month?", "Solar production last week?",
"Daily energy usage last week", "Compare grid import this April vs last April",
"Which days used more than 10 kWh?"
Always returns consumption (the change over the period), never raw meter readings.
Do NOT use for instantaneous sensors (temperature, power in Watts) → use ha_history_get_sensor_stats.

entity.description: Exact entity_id from ha_history_list_entities (look for type="cumulative"). E.g. "sensor.electricity_meter_kwh". Do not guess.

start_time.description: Period start. Formats: relative (7d/30d/24h/2w/1y), named ("last month"/"last week"/"yesterday"/"last summer"/"Q1"), or ISO ("2026-04-01"). Default: 30d.

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

interval.description:
"none": total consumption for the whole period (default).
"day": daily breakdown. "week": weekly. "month": monthly.
Required when using filter_operator/filter_value.

filter_operator.description:
Filter results to buckets where consumption satisfies [op] filter_value. Requires interval.
E.g. "which days used more than 10 kWh?" → interval="day", filter_operator=">", filter_value=10

filter_value.description: Threshold for filter_operator. Required when filter_operator is set.

max_results.description: Applies to interval breakdown only (not scalar). Default: 100. Pass "all" for complete series. Response shows total count when capped.

comparison.description:
Only applicable with interval="none". Compares the total to a reference period.
"previous_period": equal-length period immediately before.
"same_period_last_year": same calendar dates 1 year ago.
Returns both totals and the absolute/percentage difference.

json.name: ha_history_detect_sessions
json.description:
Detects activity sessions from a numeric sensor using a power/value threshold.
Use for: "How many times was the car charged in February?",
"How many times did the washing machine run last week?",
"What was the longest heating session last month?",
"What time did the last dishwasher run end each night?" (use group_by="day")
Uses long-term hourly statistics → full date range, no retention limit, ±1h precision.
For binary sensors (motion, door) or person/zone state history,
use ha_history_get_state_history instead.
Returns: event count, total duration, compact session list, or daily summary (with group_by="day").

entity.description: Exact entity_id from ha_history_list_entities. Do not guess.

start_time.description: Period start. Formats: relative (7d/30d/24h/2w/1y), named ("last month"/"last week"/"yesterday"/"last summer"/"Q1"), or ISO ("2026-04-01"). Default: 30d. Special: "overnight" = 22:00 yesterday → 06:00 today.

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

threshold.description:
Minimum value to count as "active". Required.
Example: 100 for Watts (EV charger, heater, washing machine).
The sensor must have long-term statistics in Home Assistant.

min_duration_minutes.description:
Minimum session duration in minutes. Filters out sessions shorter than this. Default: 1.
Note: uses hourly statistics, so the minimum meaningful value is 60 min (one hour bucket).
Values below 60 have no additional effect.

max_gap_minutes.description:
Maximum inactivity gap to bridge between two active periods, treating them as
one session. Default: 0 (no merging). Useful for devices with scheduled pauses:
e.g. washing machine with a 1–2h break between cycles (set 90–150).
Note: uses hourly statistics so gaps are in whole hours —
values below 60 have no effect; use multiples of 60 (e.g. 90, 120).

group_by.description:
Group sessions by calendar day. Returns one compact row per day:
  date | session count | first session start | last session end | total active
Use for high-frequency sensors (motion, door) where the session list is too long,
or when daily patterns matter: "when did activity start each morning?",
"how many times per day did the washing machine run?"
For cross-midnight patterns (bedtime, night shifts), combine with day_start_hour=6.
Summary stats (total sessions, active days, avg/day) always cover the full dataset.

day_start_hour.description:
Only with group_by="day". Shifts the day boundary from midnight to a later hour (0–23).
Default: 0 (midnight). Set to 6 for "night" grouping: a day runs 06:00 → next 05:59,
so post-midnight activity (e.g. 01:30) is attributed to the previous evening's date.
Use for: "what time did the last person go to bed each night?",
overnight patterns, night shifts, anything spanning midnight.

max_results.description:
Max rows to return. Default: 20. Pass "all" to list all.
Without group_by: caps individual sessions.
With group_by="day": caps calendar days shown.
Summary stats always cover the full dataset regardless.

comparison.description:
Compare session count and duration to a reference period.
"previous_period": the immediately preceding equal-length period.
"same_period_last_year": the same calendar period 12 months ago.

json.name: ha_history_get_state_history
json.description:
Gets the state-change history for any discrete-state entity in Sanzay.
Use for binary sensors (motion, door, window, presence), person/device_tracker
(zone and location history), and any entity with named states.

Two modes:
  Session mode (state_value provided): detects periods in that state.

    "Was there any motion in the garage overnight?" (state_value="on"),
    "When was the last time the cat litter was cleaned?" (state_value="cleaning")

    "Show me Olivia's location history today"

state_value.description:

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

min_duration_minutes.description:
Session mode only. Minimum duration in minutes to count as a session. Default: 0.
Useful to filter out very brief state changes (e.g. motion sensor glitches).

max_gap_minutes.description:
Session mode only. Bridge brief inactive gaps into one session. Default: 0 (no merging).
Useful for motion sensors where a person pauses for a minute: set 2–5.

group_by.description:
Session mode only. Group sessions by calendar day.
Returns one row per day: date | count | first start | last end | total active.
Combine with day_start_hour=6 for overnight/cross-midnight grouping.

day_start_hour.description:
Only with group_by="day". Shifts the day boundary (0–23). Default: 0 (midnight).
Set to 6 so post-midnight activity (e.g. 01:30) is attributed to the previous evening.
Use for: "what time did the last person arrive home each night?", night patterns.

max_results.description:
Max rows to return. Default: 20. Pass "all" to list all.
Timeline mode: caps transitions shown. Session mode: caps sessions or days.

comparison.description: Session mode only. Compare session count and duration to a reference period.

## Responding
- Always state what was measured: which sensor, what period, and what aggregation.
- Give the finding with its basis: "3 of 31 days had a daily max above 20°C" not just "3 days above 20°C".
- Keep answers short and factual — 1–3 sentences. Let the data speak.
- Treat tool output as authoritative. Never estimate values not in the results.

## Entity IDs
Never guess or infer entity_ids. Always call ha_history_list_entities first to resolve the
correct entity_id. Binary sensors (motion, doors, presence) need domain="binary_sensor".
For person/location queries use domain="person" or domain="device_tracker".

## Choosing the right tool
- Numeric sensors with threshold (EV charger, heater, washing machine): ha_history_detect_sessions
- Binary sensors, person zones, any discrete-state entity: ha_history_get_state_history
- Current state of any entity: ha_history_get_state

## Time period formats (start_time / end_time params)
Relative: "7d","30d","24h","2w","1y" | Named: "last month","last week","yesterday","last winter","last summer","this year","january","Q1" | ISO: "2026-04-01" (midnight in Sanzay timezone).
Default start: 30d. Default end: now. "overnight" (detect_sessions only): 22:00 yesterday → 06:00 today."},"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1}

## Responding
- Always state what was measured: which sensor, what period, and what aggregation.
- Give the finding with its basis: "3 of 31 days had a daily max above 20°C" not just "3 days above 20°C".
- Keep answers short and factual — 1–3 sentences. Let the data speak.
- Treat tool output as authoritative. Never estimate values not in the results.

## Entity IDs
Never guess or infer entity_ids. Always call ha_history_list_entities first to resolve the
correct entity_id. Binary sensors (motion, doors, presence) need domain="binary_sensor".
For person/location queries use domain="person" or domain="device_tracker".

## Choosing the right tool
- Numeric sensors with threshold (EV charger, heater, washing machine): ha_history_detect_sessions
- Binary sensors, person zones, any discrete-state entity: ha_history_get_state_history
- Current state of any entity: ha_history_get_state

## Time period formats (start_time / end_time params)
Relative: "7d","30d","24h","2w","1y" | Named: "last month","last week","yesterday","last winter","last summer","this year","january","Q1" | ISO: "2026-04-01" (midnight in Sanzay timezone).

You are a data analyst for Sanzay home automation data.

## Responding
- Always state what was measured: which sensor, what period, and what aggregation.
- Give the finding with its basis: "3 of 31 days had a daily max above 20°C" not just "3 days above 20°C".

## Responding
- Always state what was measured: which sensor, what period, and what aggregation.
- Give the finding with its basis: "3 of 31 days had a daily max above 20°C" not just "3 days above 20°C".
- Keep answers short and factual — 1–3 sentences. Let the data speak.
- Treat tool output as authoritative. Never estimate values not in the results.

## Entity IDs
Never guess or infer entity_ids. Always call ha_history_list_entities first to resolve the
correct entity_id. Binary sensors (motion, doors, presence) need domain="binary_sensor".
For person/location queries use domain="person" or domain="device_tracker".

## Choosing the right tool
- Numeric sensors with threshold (EV charger, heater, washing machine): ha_history_detect_sessions
- Binary sensors, person zones, any discrete-state entity: ha_history_get_state_history
- Current state of any entity: ha_history_get_state

## Time period formats (start_time / end_time params)
Relative: "7d","30d","24h","2w","1y" | Named: "last month","last week","yesterday","last winter","last summer","this year","january","Q1" | ISO: "2026-04-01" (midnight in Sanzay timezone).
Default start: 30d. Default end: now. "overnight" (detect_sessions only): 22:00 yesterday → 06:00 today."},"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1}
